diagnosis: The previous fixture selected its main listener with UDP port zero, without proving the same number was available to TCP. TLS was selected and released independently. Linux reproduction confirms that a TCP TIME_WAIT port can remain available to UDP while native TCP binding correctly refuses it. The exact conflicting socket in the hosted failure was not captured.
fixture_changes: Reserve one TCP and UDP listener number together, and a distinct optional TLS TCP number, while all reservations remain held.
Choose generated unprivileged listener numbers outside the usual client ephemeral ranges used by the test hosts.
Release reservations immediately before launch; retry only an observed EADDRINUSE hand-off collision, at most eight attempts within a ten-second readiness deadline.
Bound certificate generation and startup output, read partial stderr without blocking, and close/reap failed children.
regressions: TCP/UDP reservations remain held and TLS differs.
Occupied TCP or UDP candidates are skipped.
A forced hand-off collision recovers and the failed child is reaped.
A non-bind configuration failure is rejected without retry.
A partial startup line obeys the deadline and the child is reaped.
